notes.summary: A statement is followed by conclusions or assumptions. Treat the statement as true and decide what definitely follows from it (conclusion) or what the speaker takes for granted (assumption). 0–2 questions.

concepts.title: Conclusion
concepts.body: A conclusion follows only if it can be directly drawn from the statement. Words like "only", "all", "always", "never" usually make a conclusion too strong.

concepts.title: Assumption
concepts.body: An assumption is something the speaker believes before making the statement; without it the statement would not make sense. An advertisement assumes people will read it and want the product.

varieties.name: Statement and conclusion
varieties.how: Ask: is this definitely true from the given facts alone?

example.q: Statement: 25% of students failed. Conclusion: 75% passed.

varieties.name: Statement and assumption
varieties.how: Ask: why would anyone say this? What must they believe?

example.q: Notice: "Keep the lights off when not needed."
steps: The writer assumes people will read and follow it.
The writer assumes saving power is useful.

tips: Do not add outside facts; stay inside the statement.
Extreme words (only, all, never, definitely) usually make a conclusion or assumption fail.
traps: A conclusion can be reasonable in real life but still not follow from the statement.
A repeated fact from the statement does follow as a conclusion.

questions.q:
Statement: Regular exercise keeps the body fit.
Conclusions:
I. People who exercise regularly are generally fit.
II. Only exercise can keep a person fit.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution:
I restates the statement: follows.
II adds "only"; the statement does not say other ways (diet, sleep) fail. II does not follow.

questions.q:
Statement: "Use XYZ toothpaste for whiter teeth." — an advertisement.
Assumptions:
I. People want whiter teeth.
II. People read or notice advertisements.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.solution:
The advert promises whiter teeth, so it assumes people want them (I).
An advert is made only if people notice adverts (II).
Both are implicit.

questions.q:
Statement: The government has made helmets compulsory for pillion riders on two-wheelers too.
Conclusions:
I. Head injuries to pillion riders are a concern.
II. All pillion riders will stop travelling on two-wheelers.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution:
A safety rule for pillion riders shows their head injuries are a concern: I follows.
Nothing suggests people will stop travelling: II does not follow.

questions.q:
Statement: The school has decided to hold extra classes for weak students on Saturdays.
Assumptions:
I. Extra classes will help weak students improve.
II. Weak students do not want to come to school on Saturdays.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.solution:
The school would arrange extra classes only if it believes they help: I is implicit.
II goes against the plan; the school assumes students will attend. II is not implicit.

questions.q:
Statement: Of the 1,200 students who took the test, only 300 passed.
Conclusions:
I. The test was too difficult.
II. 25% of the students passed the test.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution:
300/1200 = 1/4 = 25%: II follows.
Low results may be due to poor preparation or many other reasons; I does not definitely follow.

questions.q:
Statement: A teacher tells students, "If you want to score well in the exam, solve previous years' papers."
Assumptions:
I. Previous years' papers help students understand the exam pattern.
II. Students want to score well.
options: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.solution:
The advice makes sense only if old papers are useful (I) and students care about scoring well (II).
Both are implicit.

flashcards.back: Is it definitely true from the statement alone?
Would the statement make sense if this were false? If not, it is implicit.
